event.name: UFC 333: Volkanovski vs. Evloev
event.notes: "mode": "auto" means every run resolves this itself — before config.json is even loaded, it asks ESPN for the soonest upcoming card, and if that differs from "name" below it rewrites "name"/"league"/"date", regenerates discovery.title_contains and discovery.search.queries from the new main event's fighters, and clears tracker.picks_videos (a stale roundup URL would just burn a download and a vision pass on the old event's deck). Once this week's card has happened, the next run rolls to whatever's next on its own — no manual retarget. "name"/"league"/"date" below are simply the last-resolved event; edit them by hand only if you delete "mode" and want to pin a specific card again (e.g. a Contender Series week, matched as a substring against ESPN's own event name — punctuation and case ignored, spelling not). "league" pins which scoreboard is searched (ufc / pfl); leave it empty to try UFC then PFL. Add more cards to the top-level "events" array to cover them in the same run — a PFL event the same weekend, say — and the dashboard puts a card selector at the top. If a run logs "No ESPN card found" (or, in auto mode, "No upcoming event found"), something's off with the league or the scoreboard is unreachable — nothing is filtered and off-card fights come back.

notes: Featherweight title, main event, five rounds. Evloev is 20-0 and 10-0 in the UFC, all by decision.

The host's third best bet, and the biggest odds-versus-picks gap on the card: the books call it a pick'em at -111/-106 while the channels are 72% Volkanovski and every sharp panel has him around 80%. Volkanovski by decision pays +185.
Bantamweight title, co-main, five rounds — the Yan/Dvalishvili trilogy.
The host's second best bet, on the moneyline: Yan at -155 is 82% of the field and 10 of 11 best predictors. Not one channel picked a submission.
The decision price came through the transcript garbled ("plus 1030"); +130 is the reading that fits a -155 favorite. Re-check it at your book.
Heavyweight. The host gave Kuniev's best-underdog-picker count only as "about a third" without a number, so that panel is left out rather than guessed at.
Flyweight, and the closest fight on the card in odds at -112/-108. Close everywhere: 50-42 in the field, 6-5 among the best predictors, dead even among the best favorite-pickers.

notes: Light heavyweight. All 92 channels and every panel are on Yakhyaev, and not one vote has it going to the scorecards.
Light heavyweight featured prelim. The host's first best bet: every panel on Murzakanov, all 7 best method predictors on the KO at -125 rather than the -215 moneyline.
Middleweight. Vagaev has 20 decision wins in 25; 89% of the method votes here are decisions.
Featherweight; opens the main card. The field has Keita by KO at 58% of the method vote, while every best method predictor has Pico — the sharpest method disagreement on the card.
Bantamweight; Chopurov's UFC debut at 11-0 and the biggest favorite on the card at -585.
Lightweight; opens the regular prelims.
Lightweight.

FLAG — two numbers here are less certain than the rest of the card. The moneyline denominator came through the transcript as a garbled word; 89 fits the host's "well over 75%" and the surrounding fights, but 88 would too. The method split was given without a total, so the usual reconciliation check could not run; 65 is the sum of the counts he read out.
The field is 76% Steele while the best predictors are 6/11 and the best underdog-pickers are 6/11 the other way — one of the widest field-versus-sharps gaps on the card.
Middleweight. The field is 62% Rowston but both sharp panels and the oddsmakers lean Magomedov.

Women's strawweight, first of the early prelims. The host said every best method predictor had Lucindo by decision but never gave the panel's size for this fight, so no method-panel count is recorded.
Featherweight, priced as a coin flip.
FLAG — the host gave this method split without stating its total, so the reconciliation check could not run; 62 is the sum of the counts he read out.
